messages.author: d9ec245234a3bd75
messages.subject: cofactors in mqm
parts:
Hello,
I have been working through the mqm tutorial for the R/qtl package and was wondering if anyone could clarify the use of 'cofactors'?
I understand that they are genetic markers (or QTL) and treated as covariates, but what is the benefit to using cofactors instead of not using them? Does including cofactors allow you to detect QTL that would otherwise be undetected?

Thanks for the help!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] cofactors in mqm
parts:
Yes, the use of cofactors is to try to reduce residual variation due, to potentially enhance the power to detect QTL.

karl

parts:

messages.author: d9ec245234a3bd75
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] cofactors in mqm
parts:
That makes sense for an F2, but we have incompletely inbred lines. Therefore, we are restricting our dataset to bi-allelic SNPs (most are biallelic anyway) when using the F2 cross input. 

So, can we use phase information from our linkage mapping results (1s and 0s for each marker)?  If coding for an f2 cross can not reflect phase then how would one use phase information for e.g. a CP population cross? I know the codings are numerous for CP, but how would you input phase with those codings?  In the rQTL manual there are many references to “phase known” crosses or data , which we have, but how to include in rQTL when inputting said data?

Thank you!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] cofactors in mqm
parts:
R/qtl includes a "phase-known four-way cross" as a cross type, "4way". It's assuming a cross between four inbreds (AxB)x(CxD).
Coding of genotypes is rather complicated and is described in the help file to read.cross.

karl
